lecture_15.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 15: "After pretraining" (mid/post-training): SFT, RLHF data, PPO, DPO
lecture_15.anchor_convention: lecture_15.pdf:p<page>, page numbers from `pdftotext -layout` form feeds (title slide = p1; p66 is an empty trailing page)
lecture_15.note: Evidence is the text layer of the slides (lecture_15.txt), extracted page-by-page by discover_slides.py (sha256 of txt in discovered.json). The deck is screenshot-heavy: the InstructGPT pipeline figure (p6, p31), the response-length and length-bias plots (p16-p17, p48), the Schulman/Gekhman hallucination figures (p20), the safety-tuning plots (p26), the mid-training recipe figure (p29-p30), the G-V gap figure (p33), the pairwise-feedback setup and InstructGPT guideline (p36-p37), the annotator-demographics and annotator-variation plots (p43-p44), the GPT-4-as-judge agreement plots (p45), the InstructGPT PPO objective and the Stiennon reward-model loss (p51-p52), the whole DPO derivation (p56-p58), the Tulu 3 variant losses (p60), the PPO-vs-DPO tables (p61), the overoptimization curves (p63) and the calibration plot (p64) are images; only their captions survive in the text layer. Numbers visible only in those images are recorded in filtering_note, never in statements or prompts.

lecture_16.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 16: Post-training 2, reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards
lecture_16.note: Next deck (atlas thread atlas/lectures/lecture_16). It expands the PPO sketch of p53 (lecture_16:policy-gradient-variance, lecture_16:ppo-ratio-clip, lecture_16:per-token-kl-reward-shaping), rejects PPO and DPO for verifiable rewards (lecture_16:why-grpo-not-ppo-or-dpo) and takes the overoptimization warning of p62-p63 as its motivation (lecture_16:verifiable-reward-vs-rlhf). Forward links from this thread use see_also and external_prerequisites with ids lecture_16:<kp-id>; no quotes are anchored into it.

instructgpt.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (Ouyang et al., 2022; InstructGPT)
instructgpt.note: Cited as [Ouyang 2022] on p6 and p31 (the SFT -> reward model -> PPO pipeline figure) and 'From InstructGPT' on p51 (the PPO objective with the KL penalty to the SFT model and the pretraining-mix term; image-only). p37 shows the InstructGPT annotation guideline as a screenshot.

stiennon_2020_summarize.title: Learning to summarize from human feedback (Stiennon et al., 2020)
stiennon_2020_summarize.note: p5 ('Stiennon 2020 (RLHF paper) - contains annotation guidelines'), p52 ('From "Learning to summarize from human feedback"', background and the pairwise reward-model loss as an image) and p57 ('the Stiennon objective', the Bradley-Terry log-sigmoid loss that DPO re-parametrizes). The Bradley-Terry form p(y_w > y_l) = sigmoid(r(y_w) - r(y_l)) itself is image-only in the deck.

openassistant.note: p9 progression, p12 random examples (human-written, detailed, with references), p14 ('OASST goes into much more detail about various factual pieces of knowledge') and p19 (the monopsony example with a Bivens & Mishel citation).

tulu3.title: Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training (Lambert et al., 2024)
tulu3.note: p9 progression, p46 (UltraFeedback-style AI feedback used in Tulu 3) and p60 ('two of note from the Tulu 3 paper': SimPO and length-normalized DPO, losses image-only). Aloud (30:32-31:50) p24-p25 are Tulu 3's safety pipeline: unsafe requests and jailbreaks mined from WildChat, 'something like 50,000-ish examples' (spoken, not cross-checked).
